chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Mufrid (one who performs Hajj al-Mufrid): does he advance his Tawaf or delay it? He said, 'He advances it.'
A man beside him said, 'But my Sheikh did not do that; when he arrived, he stayed in Fakh until the people departed for Mina, then he departed with them.'

So I asked him, 'And who is your Sheikh?' He said, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both).' So I inquired about the man, and it turned out he was the half-brother of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) from the mother's side.

key_terms.بِفَخٍّ: In Fakh: a location near Mecca where pilgrims would stay
key_terms.طَوَافَهُ: Tawaf: the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.مُفْرِدِ الْحَجِّ: Mufrid: one who performs Hajj al-Mufrid, entering Ihram for Hajj alone without Umrah
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina: the plain near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj days

ai.seo_question: When should a Mufrid perform their Tawaf during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights a nuanced juristic difference (ikhtilaf) regarding the timing of Tawaf al-Qudum for the Mufrid, contrasting Imam al-Baqir’s directive to advance it with the practice of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who delayed it until after the crowd dispersed to Mina. The mention of the companion being the half-brother of the Imam underscores the close transmission of these specific ritual nuances within the Ahl al-Bayt's circle, reflecting the practical wisdom of avoiding congestion during the sacred rites.
